Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second chapter to unfold! The Umpires are ready with their positions and so are the players of Bangladesh. Muhammad Zohaib and Muhammad Waseem will be opening for United Arab Emirates. Tanzim Hasan Sakib will bowl with the new ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Following the dismissal of Hrindoy shortly after the drinks break, it appeared that the UAE team was beginning to regain momentum in the match. However, their hopes were short-lived, as the promising 22-year-old continued his innings despite witnessing his partners lose their wickets. The narrative took an intriguing turn when Matiullah Khan claimed the wicket of Emon in the 17th over; however, it was unfortunate that he had overstepped on that delivery, granting a fortunate reprieve to the batter, which the bowling side regretted later in the inning. However, Muhammad Jawadullah is the top bowler from United Arab Emirates, picking four wickets and only giving 21 runs. Other bowlers leaked many boundaries and failed to keep the batters on pressure. But we have witnessed some outrageous comebacks in chasing inning, especially in this format of cricket. So stick with us as the second inning might start in no time.

Parvez Hossain Emon is up for a chat and says that it was his first century in international cricket and is really happy for it. Adds that his teammate had faith in him and he tried his best. Mentions that the Bangladeshi supporters are always with the team and help him perform better.

Bangladesh was unsuccessful in achieving the desired start in this fast-paced format of cricket, suffering the loss of two top-order batters during the powerplay. Nonetheless, commendation is warranted for Parvez Hossain Emon, who assumed responsibility during this challenging phase. He entered the match as an opener and remained on the pitch until the conclusion of the innings. Furthermore, Tawhid Hridoy provided essential support, and together they established a partnership that produced 58 runs off merely 32 deliveries. But other than him, no other bowlers were economical.

What an extraordinary inning we just experienced! The fervent supporters of Bangladesh must be celebrating as their team undeniably showcased their dominance during the first inning. However, it is Parvez Hossain Emon who truly deserves a standing ovation from cricket aficionados everywhere. His brilliant display of stroke play culminated in a stunning 100 runs off just 54 deliveries, propelling his team to an impressive total of 191 runs. What a remarkable performance!

Finishes well, does Muhammad Jawadullah! Hard length again and outside off, Tanzim Hasan Sakib swings across the line but misses and goes nowhere as the keeper scores a direct hit at the batter's end. A dot to end and Bangladesh finish with 191/7 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: We are underway to start the clash! The Umpires are heading towards their respective positions and so are the fielders of United Arab Emirates. Tanzid Hasan will be pairing with Parvez Hossain Emon as the openers for Bangladesh. Dhruv Parashar will get the job to start with the new ball. Here we go...

We are moments from the start of the match but before that, both sets of players line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first, followed by the national anthem of United Arab Emirates.

Litton Das, skipper of Bangladesh, starts by saying he is blessed to have an opportunity to lead his nation, but at the same time, he knows that he needs to focus on the games. About the toss, he is happy to bat first as the track looks good to him. He believes that if they bat well and post a big target, it will be effective in the second inning because the wicket will get slower. Ends up saying that they are trying hard to improve their weak points and he is hopeful that they will bring some positive results.

The captain of United Arab Emirates, Muhammad Waseem, says they are going to bowl first. Observes that the pitch looks good and fresh as it hasn't been used for the last four to five months. Adds that, the pitch will help our bowlers and that's why he has chosen to field first. Mentions that they will aim to restrict them to a low total between 140 and 150. Shares that, the players are used to these conditions and everyone is ready. Informs that they have three debutants today.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das (C), Parvez Hossain Emon, Tanzid Hasan, Tawhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali (WK), Shamim Hossain, Mahedi Hasan, Tanvir Islam, Hasan Mahmud, Mustafizur Rahman, Tanzim Hasan Sakib

United Arab Emirates (Playing XI) - Muhammad Waseem (C), Muhammad Zohaib, Alishan Sharafu, Rahul Chopra (WK), Asif Khan, Dhruv Parashar, Sanchit Sharma, Muhammad Zuhaib, Matiullah Khan, Haider Ali, Muhammad Jawadullah.
TOSS - United Arab Emirates have won the flip of the coin and opted to FIELD first.

Bangladesh, under the new leadership of Litton Das, aims to find the right balance and method ahead of the upcoming ICC T20 World Cup. The team has made a strong comeback with quality players like Tawhid Hridoy, Tanvir Islam, Mustafizur Rahman, and Shoriful Islam. Although Afif Hossain and Mehidy Hasan Miraz are absent, and Taskin Ahmed is dealing with an achilles injury, Bangladesh's strengthened squad will be hoping to put up a strong fight against the UAE. With talented stars on both sides, a close contest is expected. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

United Arab Emirates, led by seasoned captain Muhammad Waseem, is riding high on confidence after winning the Gulf Cricket Championship 2024. Waseem's leadership and experience will be crucial as they take on Bangladesh. The UAE squad retains its core players, including Alishan Sharafu, Rahul Chopra, and Muhammad Jawadullah. Skipper Waseem, Alishan, and Asif Khan have been in form, scoring runs in the recently concluded ODI tri-series, and the team will be counting on them to deliver.

Cricket enthusiasts are in for a treat as the United Arab Emirates and Bangladesh lock horns in a thrilling two-match T20I series at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium. This series promises to deliver crackerjack action and exciting moments, with both teams vying for dominance.
... MATCHDAY ...

Sharjah lights up once again as cricket returns with a fresh buzz - it's the opening T20I between United Arab Emirates and Bangladesh, and both sides have a point to prove. For the hosts, it’s about showing they belong on the big stage, for the visitors, it’s about asserting dominance and testing depth ahead of bigger battles to come. With pride, momentum, and opportunity all on the line, expect a fiery start to this short but significant series. UAE, led by the dependable Muhammad Waseem, will rely on their familiarity with conditions to challenge their more experienced opponents. Waseem’s attacking instincts, paired with the likes of Alishan Sharafu and Asif Khan, could give their top order some bite. Muhammad Zuhaib’s leg-spin will be crucial in the middle overs, and Matiullah Khan’s pace threat gives them teeth with the new ball. Bangladesh, meanwhile, arrive with a balanced squad that blends seasoned heads with exciting talent. Skipper Litton Das will lead from the front with the bat, while Soumya Sarkar and Tawhid Hridoy, and Jaker Ali adds firepower in the batting. Mahedi Hasan  brings all-round value, and Mustafizur Rahman’s experience will be key with the ball. Supporting him are Tanvir Islam and Rishad Hossain - young bowlers eager to make a mark. Bangladesh may walk in as favourites, but UAE have the belief and the crowd behind them. With both teams hungry to start strong, this promises to be more than just a formality - it’s a battle of intent and momentum, under the Sharjah lights.
